transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (Aurora CISO), Sara Lopez (Aurora Sec Eng), Tom Becker (Aurora IT Ops)

[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna do a SOC two and ISO posture review, go over trust center reports, mapping, RBAC, KMS, that sort of thing. quick round robin intro? 
[00:00:12] Michael Chen: Michael Chen, CISO at Aurora. i'll kick off with our ask: we are in the middle of our vendors tpm and need evidence for SOC2 and ISO. want to understand if you provide trust center access and how controls map to our requirements.
[00:00:28] Sara Lopez: Sara Lopez, security engineer. i'll be doing the evidence collection. i care about logs, retention, encryption keys and integration with our okta.
[00:00:36] Tom Becker: Tom Becker, infrastructure. i'll look at network, vpc peering, allow lists.
[00:00:41] Jordan Lee: Great thanks. Priya, want to take us through the high level posture and what we can share?
[00:00:47] Priya Rao: Sure. so Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. we provide a Trust Center url where customers can request access to the SOC 2 report, ISO attestation, penetration test summary (redacted), and supplemental controls matrix. access is via request and we typically grant view/download for an authorized security contact. the reports are the standard ones — Type II covers control operating effectiveness over a period. 
[00:01:15] Michael Chen: Can you confirm the period for the last Type II? like fiscal months covered.
[00:01:19] Priya Rao: last Type II period was April 1 2025 through March 31 2026. the report will be labeled accordingly. i can put the exact link in slack after the call.
[00:01:30] Sara Lopez: good. do you provide a controls mapping to ISO 27001 clause numbers? we need to map vendor controls to our control set.
[00:01:36] Priya Rao: yes we have a controls mapping csv that maps SOC2 controls to ISO 27001 controls and also to NIST 800-53 high level. it's in the trust center as a supplemental artifact. we'll share a template so you can attach evidence references. 
[00:01:53] Tom Becker: on the technical side, we need audit logs for our PoC — can we get temporary access or exported logs? also what about syslog/siem integrations?
[00:02:03] Jordan Lee: our standard practice is to provide log extracts or log-forwarding via syslog or S3 delivery for customers on dedicated/private deployments. for hosted customers we provide redacted audit logs and an API for log queries. Priya can explain specifics.
[00:02:17] Priya Rao: for hosted accounts we expose audit logs via the console and an export endpoint. the logs include account-level events, admin actions, API calls, model deployments, and authentication events. sensitive fields are redacted. retention defaults to 90 days on the hosted plan and can be extended with enterprise add-ons. for dedicated/private we support direct forward to your SIEM (S3, syslog, or Kafka). 
[00:02:42] Sara Lopez: retention policy 90 days by default — can that be configured to 365 for us? our compliance requires 1 year for vendor logs.
[00:02:49] Priya Rao: enterprise add-on supports 365 retention, yes. we'll need to scope storage costs in the quote. we can also do an on-prem archive connector if you want to keep copies in your bucket.
[00:02:59] Michael Chen: ok good. about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. does Redwood support SCIM and SAML SSO for role mappings and least privilege?
[00:03:11] Priya Rao: yes we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning. roles in Redwood map to RBAC policies; you can predefine admin, dev, readonly, and custom roles. SCIM can auto-provision groups, and SAML assertions can carry role claims. we also have API tokens for automation with fine-grained scopes. 
[00:03:31] Sara Lopez: does SCIM support group-to-role mapping out of the box or do we need to configure it on your side?
[00:03:36] Priya Rao: out of box we support group->role mapping via SCIM attributes; we'll walk through mappings in the controls-mapping session. for strict separation you'll want to combine SCIM provisioning with RBAC policies. 
[00:03:47] Tom Becker: encryption — at rest and in transit. do you use customer-managed keys (BYOK) or only Redwood-managed KMS?
[00:03:55] Priya Rao: we support both. for hosted accounts we default to Redwood-managed KMS. for enterprise/private we support BYOK integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault via a key-wrapping approach. BYOK can be part of dedicated/reserved capacity or private deployment contracts. we also support envelope encryption. 
[00:04:15] Michael Chen: if we use BYOK, does Redwood retain any plaintext or key material? and what about dual control and HSM attestations?
[00:04:21] Priya Rao: with BYOK we never receive your plaintext key material — you provide a key or key reference and we wrap/decrypt ephemeral data in the hardware boundary. no plaintext keys are stored. for HSM-backed keys we support HSM attestations and can provide KMS config docs and relevant audit artifacts from the trust center. 
[00:04:37] Sara Lopez: can you show where in the trust center the KMS docs live? is there a diagram of keyflows?
[00:04:42] Priya Rao: yes, there's a keyflow diagram and a KMS integration guide. i'll include direct links. for private deployments we provide architecture diagrams showing key boundaries.
[00:04:52] Jordan Lee: question on data residency — Aurora is required to keep PHI data in us-east-1. can Redwood pin resources to a region and provide contractual data residency guarantees?
[00:05:01] Priya Rao: yes. for dedicated capacity and private deployments we can host inference in a specified region or on-prem. for hosted multi-tenant we have region selection for data processing — we can route requests to us-east-1. contractual language is part of our DPA/contract addendum. 
[00:05:17] Michael Chen: incident response & breach notification SLA — what's the timeline and do you provide contact for security incidents?
[00:05:23] Priya Rao: standard incident response notifications are within 72 hours for confirmed breaches; we provide a security contact and escalation path in the trust center. for enterprise contracts we can negotiate shorter SLAs and dedicated PagerDuty integration. 
[00:05:36] Sara Lopez: pen tests — do you allow us to run an external pen test against our tenant or dedicated infra?
[00:05:42] Priya Rao: yes, we allow customer-initiated penetration tests on dedicated and private deployments with a testing window and rules of engagement. for hosted multi-tenant, we provide a redacted pentest report and typically do not allow external testing against shared infra; you can arrange a collaborative test with our security team to perform scoped testing. 
[00:06:02] Tom Becker: can we get sample logs to feed into our SIEM? specifically authentication logs and admin actions.
[00:06:08] Priya Rao: yes, we can export a subset of logs for testing. we'll arrange a temporary S3 export or an API token for log pulls. we'll coordinate scope with Tom. 
[00:06:17] Michael Chen: about audit evidence — do you provide snapshots of configuration, evidence of patching, and change management artifacts for controls? we need to link them to our control framework.
[00:06:28] Priya Rao: we provide control evidence packages that include configuration snapshots, change logs, vulnerability scan summaries, and patch windows where applicable. the controls mapping csv allows you to attach references to those artifacts. note that some docs are redacted for customer privacy. 
[00:06:45] Jordan Lee: competitor question — any differences vs other providers on evidence sharing and BYOK?
[00:06:50] Priya Rao: compared to larger hyperscalers, Redwood focuses on customer-first evidence sharing and flexible BYOK on enterprise tiers; we try to make trust assets accessible quickly via the Trust Center. customers have told us it's easier to get mappings and artifacts from Redwood than from some large providers. 
[00:07:07] Sara Lopez: one more technical detail: how granular are the admin audit events? do you log token rotations, policy changes, and model rollback events?
[00:07:15] Priya Rao: yes those are all logged — token create/rotate/revoke, RBAC policy changes, model deployments/rollbacks, and schema changes. timestamps are UTC and we include request ids for traceability. 
[00:07:29] Michael Chen: for the controls mapping session — we want to map to SOC 2 CC, ISO 27001 Annex A, and our internal policies. who will lead that session?
[00:07:38] Jordan Lee: Priya will lead technical mapping, and i'll coordinate commercial artifacts. we'll invite Aurora's security team. propose week of dec 14 for 60-minute workshop. 
[00:07:47] Priya Rao: i'll prepare the mapping template and pre-fill Redwood artifacts for the common controls. please send over your control list ahead of time. 
[00:07:56] Tom Becker: any ask from our side for the trust center access? like NC/PO or email alias?
[00:08:02] Jordan Lee: typically we need a signed NDA or a trust access form with an authorized security contact; jordan@redwood will send the request template. 
[00:08:12] Michael Chen: ok can you also include pen test rules of engagement and the summary report? 
[00:08:17] Priya Rao: yes pen test summary and RoE are in the trust center. full reports are redacted; if you need more details we can coordinate a call with our security team. 

[00:08:30] -- Closing and recap --
[00:08:30] Jordan Lee: Recap: 1) we'll share Trust Center link and SOC2/ISO reports (Jordan) 2) Priya will prepare controls mapping template and pre-fill key artifacts 3) we'll schedule a 60-min controls workshop week of 2026-12-14 4) arrange log export for PoC and BYOK docs if requested. 
[00:08:47] Michael Chen: sounds good, appreciate the thoroughness.
[00:08:51] Sara Lopez: thanks. i'll follow up with our control list and preferred retention requirements.
[00:08:55] Tom Becker: i'll get the network allowlist and test account info.
[00:08:58] Jordan Lee: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with links and dates. bye.
[00:09:02] End of recording.
